SUBSIDIARIES</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Hedges of Net Investments in Foreign Operations Strategy</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The Company entered into a cross-currency swap designated as a net investment hedge on November 7, 2018 to hedge the JPY currency exposure of the Company&#8217;s net investment in TOKIN. This agreement is a contract to exchange fixed-rate payments in one currency for fixed-rate payments in another currency. Changes in the fair value of this swap are recorded in equity as a component of AOCI in the same manner as foreign currency translation adjustments. In assessing the effectiveness of this hedge, the Company uses a method based on changes in spot rates to measure the impact of the foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations on both its foreign subsidiary net investment and the related swap. Under this method, changes in the fair value of the hedging instrument other than those due to changes in the spot rate are initially recorded in AOCI as a translation adjustment, and then are amortized into other (income) expense, net in the Consolidated Statement of Operations using a systematic and rational method over the instrument&#8217;s term. Changes in the fair value associated with the effective portion (i.e. those changes due to the spot rate) are recorded in AOCI as a translation adjustment and are released and recognized in earnings only upon the sale or liquidation of the hedged net investment. The terms of this cross-currency swap are as follows:</font></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:10px;padding-bottom:10px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:48px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;padding-left:24px;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#8226;</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">An amortizing cross-currency swap with an initial notional value of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">JPY 33.0 billion</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The notional amount is amortized by approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">JPY 1.4 billion</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;every six months and matures on September 30, 2024. Interest payments are made by the Company in JPY on March 31 and September 30 of each year based on the JPY notional value and a fixed rate of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">2.61%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The Company receives interest in USD on March 31 and September 30 of each year based on the USD equivalent of the JPY notional value and a fixed rate of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">6.25%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.</font></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The notional value of this contract was </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">JPY 31.6 billion</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;or </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$279.7 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;at March 31, </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Cash Flow Hedging Strategy</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Certain operating expenses at the Company&#8217;s Mexican facilities are paid in Mexican Pesos. In order to hedge a portion of these forecasted cash flows, the Company purchases foreign exchange contracts, with terms generally less than twelve months, to buy Mexican Pesos for periods and amounts consistent with underlying cash flow exposures. These contracts are designated as cash flow hedges at inception. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Unrealized gains and losses associated with the change in fair value of the foreign exchange contracts are recorded in AOCI. Changes in the derivatives&#8217; fair values are deferred and recorded as a component of AOCI until the underlying transaction is settled and recorded to the Consolidated Statement of Operations. When the hedged item affects income, gains or losses are reclassified from AOCI to the Consolidated Statement of Operations as Cost of Sales for foreign exchange contracts to purchase such foreign currency. The notional value of outstanding Peso contracts was </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$74.3 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$70.6 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;as of March 31, </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, respectively.</font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">126</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font fees, the Company has not recorded any accrual concerning the U.S. Complaints and the Canadian Complaints.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">TOKIN-Specific Legal Proceedings</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">In July 2013, TOKIN was named as </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">eight</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;defendants in </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;purported U.S. class action antitrust lawsuits (</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">In Re: Lithium Ion Batteries Antitrust Litigation</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, 13-MD-02420-YGR, United States District Court, Northern District of California) (the &#8220;Battery Class Action Suits&#8221;) regarding the sale of lithium ion batteries brought on behalf of direct product purchasers and indirect product purchasers. On March 2, 2018, TOKIN entered into a settlement agreement, which, subject to court approval, provides for the release of TOKIN and its subsidiaries from claims asserted in the Battery Class Action Suits, in consideration of which, TOKIN agreed to pay </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$2.0 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;to the settlement class of indirect product purchasers. TOKIN paid the settlement amount into an escrow account on January 25, 2019. On May 16, 2018, the Court granted final approval to a settlement agreement by which, in consideration of the release of TOKIN and its subsidiaries from claims asserted in the Battery Class Action Suits, TOKIN agreed to pay </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$4.95 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;to the settlement class of direct product purchasers. Prior to final court approval, TOKIN had paid the settlement amount into an escrow account on January 18, 2018.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Beginning in March 2014, TOKIN and certain of its subsidiaries received inquiries, requests for information and other communications from government authorities in China, the United States, the European Commission, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, and Brazil concerning alleged anti-competitive activities within the capacitor industry.&#160;</font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">133</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">KEMET CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On September 2, 2015, the United States Department of Justice announced a plea agreement with TOKIN in which TOKIN agreed to plead guilty to a one-count felony charge of unreasonable restraint of interstate and foreign trade and commerce in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act, and to pay a criminal fine of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$13.8 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The plea agreement was approved by the United States District Court, Northern District of California, on January 21, 2016. The fine is payable over </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">5 years</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">six</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;installments of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$2.3 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;each, plus accrued interest. The first </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">four</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;payments were made in February 2016, January 2017, January 2018, and January 2019, while the next payment is due in January 2020. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On December 9, 2015, the Taiwan Fair Trade Commission (&#8220;TFTC&#8221;) publicly announced that TOKIN would be fined </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">1.2 billion</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;New Taiwan dollars (&#8220;NTD&#8221;) (approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$39.5 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) for violations of the Taiwan Fair Trade Act. Subsequently, the TFTC indicated the fine would be reduced to </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">NTD 609.1 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;(approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$19.8 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">). In February 2016, TOKIN commenced an administrative suit in Taiwan, challenging the validity of the amount of the fine. On August 23, 2018, the Taipei High Administrative Court revoked the TFTC decision, finding that the decision had been time-barred by applicable statute. On September 21, 2018, the TFTC filed an appeal against the High Administrative Court's decision. Payment of the TFTC fine is not stayed during the administrative appeals; TOKIN has made installment payments of the fine aggregating to approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">NTD 152.3 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;(approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$4.9 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) as of March 31, 2019.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On March 29, 2016, the Japan Fair Trade Commission published an order by which TOKIN was fined </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">JPY 127.2 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;(approximately U.S. </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$1.1 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) for violation of the Japanese Antimonopoly Act. Payment of the fine was made on October 31, 2016.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On July 15, 2016, TOKIN entered into definitive settlement agreements in </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;antitrust suits filed with the United States District Court, Northern District of California as </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">In re: Capacitors Antitrust Litigation</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, No. 3:14-cv-03264-JD (the &#8220;Capacitor Class Action Suits&#8221;). Pursuant to the terms of the settlement, in consideration of the release of TOKIN and its subsidiaries (including TOKIN America, Inc.) from claims asserted in the Capacitor Class Action Suits, TOKIN will pay an aggregate </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$37.3 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;to a settlement class of direct purchasers of capacitors and a settlement class of indirect purchasers of capacitors. Each of the respective class payments is payable in </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">five</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;installments, four of which were paid on or before the respective due dates of July 29, 2016, May 15, 2017, May 15, 2018, and May 15, 2019. The final payment is due by December 31, 2019. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On July 27, 2016, Brazil&#8217;s Administrative Council for Economic Defense approved a cease and desist agreement with TOKIN in which TOKIN made a financial contribution of Brazilian Real </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">0.6 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;(approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$0.2 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) to Brazil&#8217;s Fund for Defense of Diffuse Rights.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On March 21, 2018, the European Commission announced a decision by which TOKIN was fined </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">EUR 8.8 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;directly (approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$10.3 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) and </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">EUR 5.0 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;(approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$5.9 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) jointly and severally with NEC Corporation, for violation of the competition laws of the European Union. Payment of the fines were made on June 28, 2018. On June 4, 2018, TOKIN filed an appeal with the General Court of the European Union, seeking annulment and/or reduction of the fines.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">As noted above, TOKIN, along with KEMET and certain of its other subsidiaries, were named as defendants in the Canadian Complaints. On May 30, 2018, TOKIN entered into definitive settlement agreement with the plaintiffs in the Canadian Complaints Pursuant to the terms of the settlement, in consideration of the release of TOKIN and its subsidiaries (including TOKIN America, Inc.) from claims asserted in the Canadian Complaints, TOKIN paid </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">CAD 2.9 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;(approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$2.2 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) to a settlement class of purchasers of aluminum and tantalum electrolytic capacitors and purchasers of products containing such capacitors. The settlement payment was made on June 27, 2018. The settlement agreement has been approved by the Quebec and Ontario courts; approval by the Supreme Court of British Columbia is pending.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On November 30, 2018, the Korean Fair Trade Commission (&#8220;KFTC&#8221;) notified TOKIN of its decision to impose an administrative fine on TOKIN of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">KRW 8.1 billion</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;(approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$7.2 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">) for violation of South Korea's Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Law. Payment of the fine is not stayed during appeal; TOKIN paid the full fine amount on February 1, 2019. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On July 2, 2018, TOKIN and TOKIN America Inc. were named as two of 20 defendants in a purported U.S. class action antitrust lawsuit,</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">&#32;In re: Inductors Antitrust Litigation</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, No. 5:18-cv-00198-EJD-NC, filed in the United States District Court, Northern District of California, regarding the sale of inductors brought on behalf of direct product purchasers and </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">134</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">KEMET CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">indirect product purchasers.
